demo.metaTitle: SupoClip Demo: Real AI Clips from a Long Video
demo.metaDescription: Watch vertical, captioned clips SupoClip generated from a long-form podcast episode, with the original timestamps, hook titles, and an explanation of each pipeline step.
demo.heading: One long podcast episode in, ready-to-post vertical clips out
demo.intro: These clips were generated by SupoClip from a public long-form video. Watch them, then jump to the exact moment in the original to see what the AI picked and how it reframed it.
demo.videoDescription: Vertical clip generated by SupoClip from "{title}" ({range}). Web preview of a {duration} clip.
demo.watchOriginal: Watch this moment in the original
demo.previewNote: About these previews. To keep this page fast, the files above are shortened ({lengths}) and downscaled to 540×960. SupoClip renders full clips at 1080×1920. We don't show virality scores or speed numbers here because one demo can't support those claims. The best test is a recording of your own.

0.title: Transcribe
0.detail: The source audio is transcribed with word-level timestamps.

1.title: Select moments
1.detail: An LLM reads the transcript in overlapping windows, proposes self-contained segments, then ranks them against each other on hook, engagement, value, and shareability.

2.title: Write a hook
2.detail: Each clip gets a short hook title, burned into the top of the frame for the first few seconds.

3.title: Reframe to 9:16
3.detail: Each shot is classified. Talking shots get a crop that tracks the speaker's face. Charts, slides, and screens, like the listener graph later in the first clip, show the full frame over a blurred background. Switches line up with the source's scene cuts.

demo.pipelineNote: Captions are timed word by word, and the active word is highlighted. The same pipeline runs in the hosted app and in a <selfHost>self-hosted install</selfHost>; the <guide>AI video clipper guide</guide> covers each stage.
demo.ctaTitle: Run it on your own video
demo.ctaBody: Paste a YouTube link or upload a file. Review the suggested clips, adjust the captions, and export for Shorts, Reels, or TikTok.

ai-video-clipper.metaTitle: AI Video Clipper for Shorts, Reels & TikTok
ai-video-clipper.metaDescription: Use SupoClip to find highlights in long videos, score promising moments, create face-aware vertical crops, add captions, and export social-ready clips.
ai-video-clipper.heading: AI video clipper for turning long videos into better shorts
ai-video-clipper.summary: SupoClip combines transcription, AI-assisted highlight detection, virality scoring, face-aware reframing, word-synced captions, and export presets in one open-source workflow.

3.2: Use presets for Shorts, Reels, and TikTok

0.heading: What an AI video clipper should automate
0.p1: The time-consuming part of short-form production is not one edit. It is repeating the same review, reframing, captioning, and export work for every source video. A useful AI clipper reduces that repetition while keeping the creator in control of the final cut.
0.p2: SupoClip starts from the source transcript, identifies candidate segments, and scores them for qualities such as hook strength, engagement, value, and shareability. The score is a review aid, not a promise that a clip will go viral.
0.bullet1: YouTube URLs and uploaded video files
0.bullet4: Editable caption styles and export formats

1.heading: How the SupoClip workflow works
1.p1: Paste a YouTube URL or upload a source file. SupoClip transcribes the recording, proposes clip boundaries, and presents the strongest candidates for review. Selected moments can then be rendered as vertical, captioned videos for short-form platforms.
1.p2: Because SupoClip is open source, teams can inspect the pipeline, choose supported hosted or local language models, and adapt processing to their own infrastructure. A hosted version is also available for creators who do not want to manage deployment.
1.link1: Step-by-step: turn a YouTube video into Shorts
1.link2: Run the pipeline yourself with Docker

2.heading: Who this is built for
2.p1: The workflow fits podcasters, educators, founders, agencies, and video teams that already produce long-form recordings and need a repeatable way to publish more short-form clips.
2.p2: It is especially useful when ownership matters: self-hosters retain control of the application and can modify the source instead of depending entirely on a closed editing platform.
2.link2: Why teams choose an open-source clipper

0.question: What is an AI video clipper?
0.answer: An AI video clipper analyzes a longer recording and assists with finding short segments, reframing them, adding captions, and preparing exports for short-form platforms.

1.question: Can SupoClip turn YouTube videos into Shorts?
1.answer: Yes. SupoClip accepts YouTube URLs, identifies candidate moments, and can render vertical, captioned clips suitable for YouTube Shorts.

2.question: Is SupoClip open source?
2.answer: Yes. The SupoClip codebase is available under the AGPL-3.0 license and can be self-hosted or modified.

open-source-video-clipper.metaTitle: Open-Source Video Clipper You Can Self-Host
open-source-video-clipper.metaDescription: SupoClip is an open-source AI video clipper for self-hosted highlight detection, face-aware vertical crops, captions, and short-form exports.
open-source-video-clipper.heading: Open-source video clipper with full control of the workflow
open-source-video-clipper.summary: Run AI-assisted video clipping on your own infrastructure, inspect the source, choose your model provider, and customize how clips are scored, captioned, framed, and exported.

0.heading: Why self-host a video clipping pipeline
0.p1: Self-hosting is useful when a team needs control over deployment, provider choice, processing limits, or product customization. Instead of sending every workflow decision through a closed platform, the application can run alongside the rest of the team's infrastructure.
0.p2: SupoClip includes a Next.js frontend, FastAPI backend, background workers, PostgreSQL, and Redis. The repository includes a Docker Compose setup so the complete application can be deployed as one stack.

1.heading: What remains your responsibility
1.p1: Open source does not mean that every dependency is free. Self-hosters provide their own compute, storage, transcription service, and language-model configuration. The tradeoff is operational responsibility in exchange for source-level control.
1.p2: Teams should also review the AGPL-3.0 license, secure their environment variables, keep dependencies updated, and monitor the worker and storage layers in production.
1.bullet4: Monitor processing jobs and generated media
1.link1: Production checklist in the self-hosting guide

2.heading: Start with Docker, customize when needed
2.p1: The quickest setup is to clone the repository, copy the environment template, add the required provider credentials, and start the stack with Docker Compose. Developers can then change the scoring logic, caption presets, interface, or deployment model as their workflow evolves.
2.p2: Creators who prefer not to operate infrastructure can use the hosted SupoClip application while keeping the open-source repository available as a migration path.

0.question: Is SupoClip free to self-host?
0.answer: The source code is free under the AGPL-3.0 license. You remain responsible for infrastructure and any paid transcription or AI-provider usage.

1.question: Can SupoClip use a local language model?
1.answer: Yes. SupoClip supports Ollama for clip selection, and TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER=whisper transcribes locally instead of calling AssemblyAI.

2.question: Does SupoClip require Docker?
2.answer: Docker Compose is the documented full-stack path. Developers can run the Next.js frontend, FastAPI API, worker, PostgreSQL, and Redis separately when their environment requires it.

youtube-shorts-clipper.metaTitle: YouTube Shorts Clipper for Long Videos
youtube-shorts-clipper.metaDescription: Turn long YouTube videos into vertical, captioned Shorts with AI-assisted highlight detection, virality scoring, and face-aware 9:16 crops.
youtube-shorts-clipper.heading: YouTube Shorts clipper for repurposing long videos
youtube-shorts-clipper.summary: Paste a YouTube URL, review AI-selected moments, and create captioned vertical clips without manually scanning and reframing the entire recording.

0.heading: How to turn a YouTube video into Shorts
0.p1: Start with a video you own or have permission to repurpose. Paste its YouTube URL into SupoClip, choose the output and caption options, and begin processing. The application transcribes the source and proposes short segments for review.
0.p2: Choose the moments that make sense without the surrounding episode. Strong Shorts usually establish context quickly, deliver one clear idea, and end without relying on footage that was removed from the clip.
0.bullet1: Use a clear spoken hook near the beginning
0.bullet2: Keep one idea per short clip
0.bullet3: Review names, numbers, and caption timing
0.bullet4: Confirm that vertical framing follows the active speaker

1.heading: Captions and vertical reframing
1.p1: SupoClip uses word-level timing to create synchronized captions and can track faces when converting landscape footage to a vertical frame. Caption templates provide a consistent starting point, while font, color, and output settings can be adjusted before rendering.
1.p2: Automated crops still deserve a visual review, especially when multiple people appear, screen shares are important, or the speaker moves quickly through the frame.
1.link1: What the AI clipper automates, stage by stage

2.heading: Build a repeatable repurposing workflow
2.p1: Treat each long video as a source library rather than a one-time upload. Process the recording, group clips by theme, and connect each Short back to the longer video or a relevant product page.
2.p2: Track which topics earn watch time and engagement, then use those results to guide future recordings. SupoClip's scores help prioritize candidates; publishing data should determine what the audience actually values.

0.question: Can I paste a YouTube URL into SupoClip?
0.answer: Yes. SupoClip supports YouTube URLs as a source for transcription, candidate selection, and clip generation.

1.question: Does SupoClip add captions to Shorts?
1.answer: Yes. It supports word-synced subtitles and configurable caption templates for generated clips.

2.question: Does every AI-selected clip perform well?
2.answer: No. AI scoring helps prioritize candidates, but creators should review context, accuracy, framing, and fit for their audience before publishing.
